summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 1, part 86) in which a narrator and his friend Jolu debug code for a program that auto-updates for hundreds of thousands of users, and the narrator proposes a secret invite rule for some game-like social challenge. The passage then shifts to a description of the Sutro Baths ruins at Ocean Beach in San Francisco, covering their 1896 opening as the largest indoor bathing house, their decline and 1966 fire, and the rough, cold, dangerous shoreline around them.
one_line: A novel excerpt blending a programming scene with Jolu and a description of the ruined Sutro Baths in San Francisco.
key_facts: The narrator and Jolu debug together, with Jolu debugging while the narrator watches over his shoulder.
The narrator says pair programming used to be called "extreme programming," which was a little embarrassing.
The passage quotes the cliche "With enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow."
The code is auto-updated in the background, and users wake up about once a week to a better program.
The narrator notes the code would be used by hundreds of thousands of people, tomorrow.
The narrator proposes that invitees can bring a maximum of one person, who must have been known personally for a minimum of five years.
The narrator recalls the Harajuku Fun Madness days, which involved social challenges with large groups of people.
Sutro Baths opened in 1896 and was, when it opened, the largest indoor bathing house in the world.
The Sutro Baths were a huge Victorian glass solarium with pools, tubs and an early water slide.
The owners torched the Sutro Baths for the insurance in 1966, after it went downhill by the fifties.
All that remains of the Sutro Baths is a labyrinth of weathered stone set into the cliff-face at Ocean Beach.
Waves rush through caves near the Sutro ruins in rough tides and have been known to drown the occasional tourist.
Ocean Beach lies past Golden Gate park beneath a stark cliff lined with expensive houses.
Seal Rock is a giant white rock off the shore that once hosted sea lions until they were relocated.
